newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit eases on strength of dollar/majors.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit eases on strength of dollar/majors.

text.p: * Ringgit eases due to strong dollar/majors
* Seen weakening over next few days
* Japanese ringgit buying fails to make an impact
The ringgit weakened beyond 2.51 a dollar in early Asian trading on the back of a surge in dollar/majors, dealers said on Monday.
"The big dollar is firmer this morning. Dollar/malay is just following suit," said a Singapore-based European bank dealer.

"The lack of a strong comment from G-7 on the yen decline is pushing up the dollar/majors," said Jimmy Koh, economist at research firm I.D.E.A. in Singapore. "We should see more ringgit losses over the next few days," he said.
Another Singapore-based European bank dealer said the ringgit was unlikely to dip sharply as some Japanese funds and Malaysian corporates were still buying the Malaysian unit.
"The strategy is to buy dollar/Malay on the dip because the market still fears Bank Negara intervention," he said.
He said Bank Negara was rumoured to be constantly checking the market, though it has not come in for the last two weeks. It had intervened to slow the ringgit's fall at 2.5120 a dollar.
Dealers said the dollar/ringgit would at best ease to 2.52 a dollar over the next few days.
"The ringgit now needs much stronger factors to move," a Kuala Lumpur-based dealer said.

He said the market was also waiting for the trade data for February, expected to be released this week. But, market expectations for the data were mixed with some predicting a surplus, while others saying it would be a deficit.
At 0230 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5130/40 a dollar.
